title: Mathematics

sourceText.admission:
Admission Requirements

The Department of Mathematics has two admission pathways: Early Entrance and Standard Entry. For either pathway, visit the Department website for instructions to declare the major.

• Early Entrance: 

• Minimum course requirements: MATH 200 (or MATH 300), MATH 208

• Grade requirements: Minimum 3.8 grade for each course required for admission

• Standard Entry: 

• Minimum course requirements: MATH 124, MATH 125, MATH 126, MATH 200 (or MATH 300), MATH 208

• Grade requirements: Minimum 2.0 grade for each course required for admission; minimum 3.20 cumulative GPA in courses required for admission

The Department of Mathematics does not accept post-baccalaureate applicants.

sections.credentialOverview:
Credential Overview

For students wanting both a strong foundation and the freedom to shape their program in Mathematics. The B.S. Mathematics- Standard Option gives students coursework in a range of Mathematics courses and is especially suited for students interested in the mathematical sciences.
sections.credentialCompletionRequirements:
Completion Requirements

70-88 credits

• Core (30-44 credits): 

• Complete one of the following: 

• MATH 124, MATH 125, MATH 126, MATH 207, MATH 208

• MATH 134, MATH 135, MATH 136*

• Complete one of the following: 

• MATH 200, MATH 224, MATH 300, MATH 327, MATH 424

• MATH 334, MATH 335, MATH 336**

• Advanced Mathematics (20-24 credits): At least six courses from the following, or five if using item b., either in two three-quarter sequences or three two-quarter sequences, with at least one sequence from items a. through d. 

• Modern Algebra: MATH 402, MATH 403, MATH 404

• Concepts of Analysis: MATH 425, MATH 426. MATH 424 counts as the first course in the sequence.

• Complex Analysis: MATH 427, MATH 428

• Topology & Geometry: MATH 441, MATH 442, MATH 443

• Optimization: MATH 407, MATH 408, MATH 409

• Combinatorics: MATH 461, MATH 462

• Numerical Analysis: MATH 464, MATH 465

• Probability: MATH 491/STAT 491 and either STAT 492/MATH 492 or MATH 493/STAT 493

Proficiency in items a. and b. is generally expected for graduate study in mathematics. In addition, items c. and d. are recommended for PhD programs in pure mathematics. Alternative combinations may be preferred for graduate study in other areas of the mathematical sciences and for industry careers. Consult Mathematics Student Services for more information.

• Electives (20-24 credits): Five or six additional mathematics courses at the 300- or 400-level from a list maintained by the Department. Courses from the Advanced Mathematics core sequences not used to fulfill that requirement may be used to fulfill the elective requirement.

• A total of 11 courses (44 credits) taken from Advanced Mathematics and Electives.

• Minimum 2.0 grade in all courses presented to satisfy mathematics major requirements. Minimum 2.00 cumulative GPA in all mathematics courses at the University, including course repeats.

• Minimum 18 credits of graded mathematics courses numbered 300 or higher taken in residence through the UW Seattle campus.

*May receive advanced placement (AP) credit for MATH 124 (after completing MATH 134) and MATH 125 (after completing MATH 135).

**MATH 335 may also be used as one upper-division elective and MATH 336 may also be used either as MATH 427 or one upper-division elective.
